# SODOTO Mutual Certification Contracts
## Three Symmetric Handshakes
### ReLocalize Creativity Network — Version 0.4 — 2026-03-06

---

## The Core Principle

Each SODOTO gate is a **symmetric handshake** between two parties.
Both must say yes. Either can say no. Neither outranks the other.

A gate does not close until both parties have affirmed.
If either party says no, the attempt ends. The process
may iterate — a new attempt can be opened — or either
party may end the certification entirely.

---

## The Three Handshakes

### Handshake 1 — See One

| Party | Assertion |
|-------|-----------|
| **Mentor** | "I showed you" |
| **Learner** | "I understood" |

The Mentor offers the showing. The Learner assesses
their own understanding. The Learner's self-assessment
is sovereign here — only the Learner knows whether
something has landed for them. The Mentor cannot declare
understanding on the Learner's behalf.

**Iterates when:** The Learner says "I did not understand."
The Mentor shows again — perhaps differently, perhaps
with more time, perhaps with new examples. This repeats
until the Learner affirms understanding, or until either
party decides to end the process.

**Ends without certification when:** The Mentor decides
not to continue showing, or the Learner decides the skill
is not for them at this time.

---

### Handshake 2 — Do One

| Party | Assertion |
|-------|-----------|
| **Learner** | "I have done one" |
| **Mentor** | "I am satisfied" |

The Learner performs the skill and asserts they have done it.
The Mentor assesses whether the performance meets their
standard. The Mentor's judgment of quality is sovereign
here — only the Mentor can say whether what they witnessed
satisfied them.

**Iterates when:** The Mentor says "I am not satisfied."
The Learner performs again — perhaps with more preparation,
perhaps in a different context, perhaps after more practice.
This repeats until the Mentor affirms satisfaction, or
until either party decides to end the process.

**Ends without certification when:** The Learner decides
not to attempt again, or the Mentor decides the standard
is not being reached.

---

### Handshake 3 — Teach One

| Party | Assertion |
|-------|-----------|
| **Learner** | "I have taught one" |
| **Mentor** | "I am satisfied with the teaching" |

The Learner teaches the skill to someone and asserts they
have done so. The Mentor witnesses the teaching and assesses
whether it met their standard. As in Do One, the Mentor's
judgment is sovereign — they must be satisfied that the
teaching was genuine and effective.

**Iterates when:** The Mentor says "I am not satisfied."
The Learner teaches again — perhaps to the same student,
perhaps to a different one. This repeats until the Mentor
affirms satisfaction, or until either party decides to end.

**Ends without certification when:** The Learner decides
not to attempt again, or the Mentor decides the teaching
standard is not being reached.

**Note on the student:** The student who receives the
teaching is not a party to this contract in the Marlowe
sense — they do not hold a role that can make contract
choices. But their experience matters. The student's
voice lives in the **narrative pages** linked to each
attempt. When the student gets a real DID, they will
co-sign a separate acknowledgement credential. The
student's satisfaction is a signal; it is the Mentor
who holds the gate.

---

## Symmetry Table

| Gate | First Assertion | Second Assertion | Iterates On |
|------|----------------|-----------------|-------------|
| See One | Mentor: "I showed you" | Learner: "I understood" | Learner says no |
| Do One | Learner: "I have done one" | Mentor: "I am satisfied" | Mentor says no |
| Teach One | Learner: "I have taught one" | Mentor: "I am satisfied" | Mentor says no |

In every case, both voices carry equal weight.
Either voice saying no keeps the gate open for another attempt.
Either voice saying "I am ending this" closes the process.

---

## Contract State Diagram

```
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │              CONTRACT CREATED                        │
  └─────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
  ┌─────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────┐
  │  HANDSHAKE 1 — SEE ONE                               │
  │                                                      │
  │  Mentor: "I showed you"  ──yes──►  Learner responds  │
  │          "I did not"     ──no───►  Close             │
  │          [timeout]                 Close             │
  │                                                      │
  │  Learner: "I understood" ──yes──►  Gate 1 closes     │
  │           "I did not"    ──no───►  Close (iterate?)  │
  │           [timeout]                Close             │
  └─────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                        │ Both yes
  ┌─────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Issuer releases See One credential                  │
  └─────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
  ┌─────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────┐
  │  HANDSHAKE 2 — DO ONE                                │
  │                                                      │
  │  Learner: "I have done one" ──yes──►  Mentor responds│
  │           "I have not"      ──no───►  Close          │
  │           [timeout]                   Close          │
  │                                                      │
  │  Mentor: "I am satisfied"   ──yes──►  Gate 2 closes  │
  │          "I am not"         ──no───►  Close (iter.?) │
  │          [timeout]                    Close          │
  └─────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                        │ Both yes
  ┌─────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Issuer releases Do One credential                   │
  └─────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                        │
  ┌─────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────┐
  │  HANDSHAKE 3 — TEACH ONE                             │
  │                                                      │
  │  Learner: "I have taught one" ──yes──►  Mentor resp. │
  │           "I have not"        ──no───►  Close        │
  │           [timeout]                     Close        │
  │                                                      │
  │  Mentor: "I am satisfied"     ──yes──►  Gate 3 closes│
  │          "I am not"           ──no───►  Close (iter?)│
  │          [timeout]                      Close        │
  └─────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┘
                        │ Both yes
  ┌─────────────────────▼────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Issuer releases full credential                     │
  │  Learner's debt to commons: RETIRED                  │
  │  Student's new debt to commons: CREATED              │
  │  Contract: Close                                     │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## Iteration Model

This Marlowe contract models **one attempt** through
all three gates. Iteration is handled by opening a new
contract instance for each attempt at a gate.

This is the correct separation of concerns:
- The contract is small, readable, and formally verifiable
- The attempt history lives in Neo4j and FedWiki
- Each attempt links to a narrative page

When a gate ends with either party saying no, the
system creates a record in Neo4j and prompts both
parties to write a narrative page about the experience.
That narrative is the learning record — not just a
pass/fail flag, but a written account of what happened
and why.

---

## Marlowe Contract Choices Summary

| Choice ID | Role | Value | Meaning |
|-----------|------|-------|---------|
| `SeeOne_MentorShowed` | Mentor | 1 | I showed you |
| `SeeOne_MentorNotShown` | Mentor | 0 | I have not shown you |
| `SeeOne_LearnerUnderstood` | Learner | 1 | I understood |
| `SeeOne_LearnerNotUnderstood` | Learner | 0 | I did not understand |
| `SeeOne_IssuerReleases` | Issuer | 1 | See One credential released |
| `DoOne_LearnerHasDone` | Learner | 1 | I have done one |
| `DoOne_LearnerNotReady` | Learner | 0 | I have not done one |
| `DoOne_MentorSatisfied` | Mentor | 1 | I am satisfied |
| `DoOne_MentorNotSatisfied` | Mentor | 0 | I am not satisfied |
| `DoOne_IssuerReleases` | Issuer | 1 | Do One credential released |
| `TeachOne_LearnerHasTaught` | Learner | 1 | I have taught one |
| `TeachOne_LearnerNotReady` | Learner | 0 | I have not taught one |
| `TeachOne_MentorSatisfied` | Mentor | 1 | I am satisfied |
| `TeachOne_MentorNotSatisfied` | Mentor | 0 | I am not satisfied |
| `TeachOne_IssuerReleases` | Issuer | 1 | Full credential released |

---

## Deadline Parameters

All deadlines are supplied at contract instantiation
via `SlotParam` named parameters, allowing different
skills and contexts to use appropriate timeframes.

| Parameter | Suggested Default | Meaning |
|-----------|------------------|---------|
| `mentor_seeone_deadline` | 30 days | Outer window for Mentor to show |
| `learner_seeone_response_deadline` | 48 hours | Learner's window after Mentor shows |
| `issuer_seeone_deadline` | 72 hours | Issuer's window after both affirm |
| `learner_doone_deadline` | 30 days | Outer window for Learner to attempt |
| `mentor_doone_response_deadline` | 48 hours | Mentor's window after Learner asserts |
| `issuer_doone_deadline` | 72 hours | Issuer's window after both affirm |
| `learner_teachone_deadline` | 30 days | Outer window for Learner to teach |
| `mentor_teachone_response_deadline` | 48 hours | Mentor's window after Learner asserts |
| `issuer_teachone_deadline` | 72 hours | Issuer's window after both affirm |

---

## Neo4j: Recording the Negotiation History

```cypher
// One attempt through the contract
(:GateAttempt {
  id:        "marc-cld-seeone-attempt-2",
  gate:      "SeeOne",
  skill:     "causal-loop-diagramming",
  date:      date("2025-10-15"),
  outcome:   "complete",   // complete | ended | timed-out
  narrative: "marc-pierson-cld-see-one-attempt-2"
})

// Mentor's assertion
(:Person {name: "Kerry Turner"})-[:ASSERTED {
  choiceId: "SeeOne_MentorShowed",
  value:    1,
  at:       datetime("2025-10-15T10:00:00")
}]->(:GateAttempt)

// Learner's assertion
(:Person {name: "Marc Pierson"})-[:ASSERTED {
  choiceId: "SeeOne_LearnerUnderstood",
  value:    1,
  at:       datetime("2025-10-15T14:23:00")
}]->(:GateAttempt)

// An earlier attempt where Learner was not ready
(:GateAttempt {
  id:        "marc-cld-seeone-attempt-1",
  gate:      "SeeOne",
  date:      date("2025-09-01"),
  outcome:   "ended",
  narrative: "marc-pierson-cld-see-one-attempt-1"
})

(:Person {name: "Kerry Turner"})-[:ASSERTED {
  choiceId: "SeeOne_MentorShowed",
  value:    1,
  at:       datetime("2025-09-01T10:00:00")
}]->(:GateAttempt)

(:Person {name: "Marc Pierson"})-[:ASSERTED {
  choiceId: "SeeOne_LearnerNotUnderstood",
  value:    0,
  at:       datetime("2025-09-01T16:00:00")
}]->(:GateAttempt)
```

---

## What This Enables

Recording every assertion — yes and no — across all
attempts gives the network data to learn from:

- How many See Ones does this skill typically require?
- Which mentors produce Learners who affirm quickly?
- Which skills have high Do One iteration rates?
- Is there a correlation between See One count and
  Teach One success?
- Which Learners tend to need more iterations — and
  does that predict anything about their teaching later?

This is the system learning about learning. Not just
certifying outcomes but observing the process by which
competence moves through a community.
